producer_report.summary: I added a small test-only crate, `athena-testkit`. Its `write_executable` writes a stand-in script through a short-lived `sh` child. The test process only writes to a pipe, so it never holds the script open for writing, and a fork in another thread cannot cause `ETXTBSY`. The six listed test sites now call it. I removed the busy-file retry from the reading test. The only `set_permissions` and `from_mode(0o755)` matches left in those files are production code. A stress test runs write-then-run cycles on 4 writer threads while 4 other threads fork. With the helper, 600 cycles produced 0 `ETXTBSY`. The in-process variant produced 18 in 600 on this machine; it prints that count with `--nocapture` and does not assert it, since it depends on scheduling. I appended D157, which says D08 was checked and stands, and added its link to `docs/decision-links.toml`. I also added the crate to `docs/architecture.md` (the policy test requires it) and to `xtask/shard-timings.txt`, and added a CHANGELOG entry. I ran fmt, clippy, the policy test and targeted tests for each changed site; all pass. I did not run the full suite.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep for `set_permissions` and `from_mode(0o755)` in xtask/src/main.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs, crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs, crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs shows no test code writing an executable stand-in itself; each such test calls the one shared helper.
criteria_check.evidence: Grep after edits: the remaining matches are production code only (xtask set_executable for git hooks at line ~808, and snapshot.rs lines 445-478 outside the tests module). All six test sites call athena_testkit::write_executable. Ran the changed tests; all pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The helper's source starts a child process (sh) with the script bytes on stdin that runs cat to a temp file, chmod 755, then mv to the final path, and waits for it; it never opens the script for writing in the test process.
criteria_check.evidence: crates/athena-testkit/src/lib.rs: WRITE_PROGRAM is `cat > "$1" && chmod 755 "$1" && mv "$1" "$2"`, run by `sh -c` with stdin piped, bytes written to the pipe, then child.wait(). No File/fs::write on the target in the process.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test` for the stress test: many write-then-exec cycles with other threads forking pass with the helper with zero ETXTBSY, and an in-process-write variant prints/records its ETXTBSY count on this machine in the test output (at least once, or the test documents how often it hit).
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-testkit -- --nocapture` printed 'helper write: 600 cycles, 0 ETXTBSY' and 'in-process write: 600 cycles, 18 ETXTBSY on this machine'. The helper test asserts zero; the in-process test prints its count (shown with --nocapture, not asserted, since it depends on scheduling) and its file doc says so.

open_issues: The in-process ETXTBSY count is non-deterministic and prints only with `-- --nocapture`. It was 18 of 600 cycles on this run. Without --nocapture the recorded output will not show it unless the test fails.
docs/architecture.md was changed although it is not on the deliverables list, because the policy test requires it.
The full `cargo test --locked` suite was not run, and is left to Athena's checks.
mistakes: I first put the shard-timings lines out of alphabetical order and then fixed them.
I first ran cargo test with two filters, which cargo rejects, and reran with one filter each.
learnings: xtask/tests/policy.rs requires every workspace crate to have a row in docs/architecture.md, so a new crate needs that edit. Dev-dependencies are not counted as edges.
A decision link's `line` must be the line of the 'Amends Dnn' phrase in docs/decisions.md. I set it to 4318 after checking with Grep.
The production ETXTBSY retry in athena-agent claude.rs (line ~45) is outside the tests and I left it alone.
desires: A way to make the in-process ETXTBSY count appear in recorded `cargo test` output without --nocapture.
